title: slicer land refuses a non-branch ref and prints root-anchored commands
findings_note: s327 relay 2026-10-17: `--branch` accepts the checked-out branch, a tag, a sha or refs/heads/NAME, so the merged check passes vacuously; the printed `git add -A .slicer` is relative to the shell's cwd while `git worktree remove PATH` is absolute
boundary: **Not in this slice:** running git writes from slicer (the allowlist stays closed).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`slicer land` checks that a branch is merged and marks its slice done, then prints the git commands to finish. Two gaps:
- `--branch` takes any ref. With the checked-out branch, a tag or a sha the ancestor check is trivially true and the printed `git branch -d` fails.
- With `slicer --root OTHER land` run from elsewhere, the printed `git add -A .slicer` points at the wrong tree.
Open question for the owner: should `land` also take `--owner`, as `done` does?

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `src/slicer/land.py`, `src/slicer/vcs.py` (a read-only `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/NAME` through the existing allowlist forms if one fits); `tests/test_land.py`; `docs/landing.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests (plus `test_Land_Owner_RecordedOnDone`); watch them go red.
2. Refuse unless `refs/heads/BRANCH` resolves and is not HEAD's branch (stable code, documented in docs/agents.md).
3. Print `git -C ROOT add -A .slicer` (or an absolute path).
4. Owner decision 2026-10-17: add `land --owner NAME`, passed to the done transition as `done --owner` does; document it in docs/landing.md.
5. CHANGELOG; mutation-check.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
